rationale: The pain is real — broken code generation from OpenAPI specs costs Rust teams meaningful hours — but solving it requires building and maintaining a high-quality code generator that deeply understands Rust's trait system, axum, and the OpenAPI spec. This is sophisticated open-source developer tooling, not a Claude-prompt-and-landing-page product. Willingness to pay is weak because developers expect code generation tools to be free or part of a larger paid platform. Operational autonomy is critically low: every new OpenAPI version, Rust edition, or axum release requires engineering maintenance.
solution_plan: Not recommended for build. A reliable Rust OpenAPI server code generator requires deep expertise in Rust's type system and ongoing maintenance as the ecosystem evolves — this is a full engineering project, not something the factory can ship in a week. The buyers (Rust backend developers) typically expect such tools to be free/open-source or bundled into a larger paid API platform. A solo non-technical operator has no realistic path to build or maintain this. Drop.
